authorizedCurrentVaultRebind.reason: Authorized already-canonical CSR delta; not one of the two producer changes.

actualImplementation: One existing producer owner now creates exactly one ephemeral RSA2048/SHA256 self-signed Code Signing identity, the documented owned-testing form in Apple TN2206. It is the sole generation path, not a fallback after any failure.

The helper writes a fixed 277-byte public request configuration in the already-owned temporary directory and selects its exact extension section. It does not inherit host v3_ca defaults or add duplicate critical OIDs; no real/user certificate shape or policy changes.

The same actual certificate bytes are the leaf and explicit code/profile test anchor. The same private key signs actual codesign output and both real embedded profile CMS layers; all profiles still name SHA256 of that actual code certificate. Original prefixes, teams, application identifiers, resource seals and entitlements are unchanged.

PKCS12 includes this one certificate and its matching private key in memory; no duplicate certfile bag. Existing stdin privacy, same owned Keychain importer/C bridge, fresh unlock/search/challenge, actual codesign command and exact detached CodeDirectory CMS checks remain required.

Original platform main/extensions/framework compile/sign, profile/DER, exact raw CMS checks and output/archive tail are byte-identical. No alternate signing backend, ad-hoc signature, global trust/search list, source-only bypass, missing-fixture skip or private-key file is added.

hypothesisAndCoverage.supportedChoice: A self-signed identity is publicly documented for testing signing machinery and needs no separate issuer certificate lookup. The prior CA-issued identity required a separate issuer; current codesign identity selection and later chain construction are not equivalent to raw key-use enumeration or an explicit-anchor trust call.
hypothesisAndCoverage.notProven: The exact deployed codesign filtering/chain/ACL cause of the prior item-not-found remains unproved. A self-signed form may still be rejected by the actual next platform run.
hypothesisAndCoverage.preservedCoverage: Existing independent owned CA+leaf fixtures, generic anchor-chain verification, production Apple authorization limitations and strict verifier algorithms are unchanged. The same-job platform fixture alone changes to a one-certificate explicit-anchor shape.
hypothesisAndCoverage.chainContract: Generic CMS permits a nonempty verified leaf-to-explicit-anchor chain of length1..16; it checks actual SecKey signature, date, networkfalse and exact last anchor. The loader passes its one real anchor to both code/profile verification. No production trust-policy change is needed to represent a length1 owned chain.
hypothesisAndCoverage.gateInputs: SDK producer remains7 existing sources; finite runner remains19 inputs. Only existing generator and portable test bytes change. Root owns the next immutable tag/full-currentcore binding; this delta changes no selection identity, budget, native test or artifact allowlist.

primaryReferences.scope: Current Apple overview says identity search checks chain trust, date and code-signing EKU; it does not expose the exact failing current codesign implementation call.

Historical official macOS guidance describes self-signed OpenSSL code signing with a named Keychain and distinguishes designated requirements from anchor trusted; it explicitly is not iOS deployment guidance.
Policy-lite filtering and full-trust filtering are separate. Full trust is required only by returnOnlyValidIdentities=true.
Published tool identity helper uses policy search with returnOnlyValidIdentities=false, resolves exact certificate SHA-1, and has no ordinary global-anchor install operation.

Published framework pre-sign context logs SecTrust evaluation failure as not fatal and still copies the certificate chain. This code cannot prove a strict-trust-only cause for the observed current CLI item-not-found.
find-identity prints separate matching(false) and valid(true) searches; its trust annotation comes from a distinct SecTrust/CSSM result evaluation.

validation.portableScope: Actual portable Python child/command/private-input boundary only; no actual OpenSSL in this suite, C/Swift compiler, Mac Keychain, codesign, SDK or native execution.

remaining: Actual new Mac finite execution must compile the unchanged importer/C bridge, import/reopen this exact one-certificate P12, codesign all four genuine SDK Mach-Os, verify every actual detached primary-CD CMS against the same explicit owned anchor and complete Keychain cleanup. No stage is assumed passed.

The actual public certificate shape and all profile/resource/entitlement/identity bindings must still pass the unchanged Swift verifier and real App SDK method in the subsequent same-source full batch.
Current macOS identity filtering, trust/ACL behavior and the prior CA+leaf item-not-found cause are not proven fixed by portable guards or the self-signed design.
No Apple account, signing-enrollment, true device install, permission, automatic renewal, cold launch, all-user-data or redistribution clearance is established.
